headline: Medium pairwise risk: shared allowlisted egress and Superset API create interaction, leakage, and compliance exposure; no direct evidence of stronger isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, with no documented shared channel or direct output ingestion. nuwa-skill has no io_surfaces, while Superset exposes only a Superset API, so a prompt-injection bridge is not evidenced. The only plausible pathway would require unusual manual bridging or external orchestration, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies nuwa-skill output into Superset prompts or API payloads, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added, the risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid copy-pasting model output into downstream prompts.
Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared MCP bridge.
Add a simple provenance label to copied text.
requires-engineering: add input sanitization and instruction-stripping at the orchestration layer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have allowlisted network egress, and Superset can call APIs; if they share a workspace or credentials, file contents or context could flow outward. Neither profile shows secrets_handled or explicit isolation, so the safer reading is that a leakage pathway exists in default deployments once shared data is introduced. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or dataset, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent is configured to send file contents through its API calls, sensitive material can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared workspace.
Use separate service accounts and API credentials.
Restrict outbound destinations to the minimum allowlist.
Review logs for accidental payload capture.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries and redaction before egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No write surfaces, filesystem permissions, or overlapping mutable-resource scopes are documented for either agent. nuwa-skill is runnable false and Superset only lists API calls, so a direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. Any conflict would require extra orchestration not shown here, making this low.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same database, git repo, or directory, conflicts become plausible.
IF Superset is configured to mutate shared resources via API while nuwa-skill also writes them, contention can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate mutable resources to each agent.
Use locking or transactional writes for shared state.
Keep nuwa-skill non-runnable unless wrapped by a controller.
Audit any shared API scopes before deployment.
requires-engineering: add concurrency control around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Superset can consume API-driven inputs, so if nuwa-skill produces analysis that is treated as authoritative, downstream actions or dashboards may reflect unchecked errors. There is no documented verification step or critique loop in either profile, and uncertainty about the exact orchestration should be resolved upward. The pathway is plausible in default integrations, so medium fits.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill output is fed into Superset without validation, errors can cascade.
IF Superset automates reporting or actions from that input, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before ingestion.
Require schema validation on all upstream outputs.
Mark generated content as untrusted in the pipeline.
Compare outputs against source data before publishing.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks and provenance tracking.

E_compliance.rationale: No sensitive data classes, residency constraints, or regulated scopes are documented for either agent. Both are open-source and docs-only, so there is no evidence of a specific compliance mismatch. Because the profiles are sparse, I cannot prove absence of mismatch, but the current record supports only a low residual compliance risk.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI, EU PII, or secrets is introduced into either agent, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policy imposes residency or retention constraints not captured in the profiles, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Confirm the data classes before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of both agents unless approved.
Document retention and deletion settings.
Review vendor and hosting residency requirements.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for residency and retention.
